I don’t have access to live market feeds right now, so I can’t pull the exact spot‑rate at this moment.  
Historically, $1 has traded somewhere between **£0.75** and **£0.80**, depending on the day’s supply/demand balance. Using a mid‑point of roughly **£0.77 per dollar** gives:

\[
\$20 \times 0.77 \;\approx\; £15.40
\]

So you’d expect around **£15–16** for $20 today—though the precise figure will shift with each tick of the foreign‑exchange markets.

If you need the most accurate number for a transaction, check a reputable source such as:
* [XE Currency Converter](https://www.xe.com/)
* Your bank’s online portal
* A financial news site (Bloomberg, Reuters)

Those sites update their rates continuously and often include fees if you’re actually converting money through a service.
